lead: Municipal markets, crafts made in Valencia and neighbourhood shops. Shopping sustainably in Valencia means supporting local producers, neighbourhood traders and a circular economy that looks after the environment.

Shopping in small businesses and neighbourhood shops that bet on healthy, environmentally friendly products is a great support for both producers and local traders. Valencia has a dense network of municipal markets that are true temples of kilometre 0, with the huerta and the Mediterranean as direct suppliers.
With the municipal markets as the stars, every neighbourhood in Valencia has its own everyday meeting place where fresh, seasonal, local produce is the absolute protagonist.

items.title: Central Market
items.subtitle: The largest temple of fresh produce in Europe
items.body: The Central Market of Valencia is one of the largest and most beautiful food markets in Europe. Its impressive Modernist building of iron, glass and ceramics, built between 1914 and 1928 and with almost 8,000 m², houses more than 300 stalls with the best produce from the Valencian huerta, the Mediterranean and local crafts. It is the temple of kilometre 0 in Valencia: oranges, artichokes, peppers, eels, seafood, cured meats and spices straight from the producer.
facts: Vegetables and fruit from the huerta
Straight from the farmers of the metropolitan area
Red prawn, cuttlefish, small rockfish and the whole Mediterranean
Longaniza, chistorra and Valencian home-made cured meats
Olives, pickled peppers, garlic and aromatic herbs

items.title: Mercado de Colón
items.subtitle: Modernist icon converted into a gourmet space
items.body: The Mercado de Colón is one of the most elegant Modernist buildings in Valencia. Designed by Francisco Mora Berenguer and opened in 1916, its structure of iron and decorative ceramics was declared a Site of Cultural Interest. Today it combines a ground floor with gourmet food stalls, florists and delicatessens with a large hospitality area along the sides. It is the market most visited by tourists for its architectural value and its quality food offering.
facts: Cheeses, Iberian cured meats, wines and high-quality delicatessen
The most beautiful in Valencia in a unique architectural setting
Cafés and restaurants with terraces along the sides of the historic building
Visit the building even if you do not buy anything: it is part of the city’s heritage

items.title: Mercado de Ruzafa
items.subtitle: The liveliest and most contemporary neighbourhood market
items.body: The Mercado de Ruzafa is the gastronomic soul of Valencia’s most vibrant neighbourhood. Its interior mixes traditional stalls of fresh fruit and vegetables with sellers of organic, gourmet and international products, reflecting the multicultural diversity of the neighbourhood. Recently renovated, the market keeps its age-old spirit of proximity, adapted to the contemporary consumer. On Mondays, the outdoor flea market fills the streets of Ruzafa with life.
facts: Stalls specialising in certified organic produce
Ingredients from all over the world for the neighbourhood’s multicultural cuisine
Clothes, costume jewellery, plants and food in the streets of Ruzafa
Produce from the Valencian huerta following the seasonal calendar

items.title: Mercado del Cabanyal
items.subtitle: The seafaring flavour of Valencia’s fishing quarter
items.body: The Mercado del Cabanyal is the market of the seafaring district par excellence, where fresh fish brought straight from the port stars at the stalls every morning. El Cabanyal, a former fishing village with unique Modernist architecture, has in its market the daily meeting point between the neighbours and the Mediterranean. On Thursdays, the Cabanyal flea market is one of the largest and most popular in the city.
facts: Brought straight from the fish auction at the port of Valencia
Clams, mussels, prawns and all the seasonal seafood
Vintage, clothes, tender garlic and second-hand goods
The spirit of the old fishing village alive at every stall

items.kicker: Plaza de Mossén Sorell · El Carmen district
items.title: Mercado de Mossén Sorell
items.subtitle: The alternative market of El Carmen
items.body: The Mercado de Mossén Sorell, in the heart of El Carmen, is the most intimate and alternative of Valencia’s municipal markets. Since its restoration, it offers a mix of traditional stalls with a more modern, artisan atmosphere. It is ideal for those looking for a quiet market without crowds, with quality produce and the charm of the bohemian neighbourhood around it. On Saturdays, the outdoor flea market turns the square into a space for crafts and second-hand goods.
facts: Traditional stalls with produce from the nearby huerta
More alternative and artisan offerings than the big markets
Crafts, alternative products and second-hand goods in the square
At the bohemian epicentre of Valencia, next to the IVAM and the Centre del Carme

items.title: Mercado del Grao
items.subtitle: The market of the old fishing district next to the port
items.body: The Mercado del Grao is the market of Valencia’s old port district, with an authentic seafaring atmosphere and an offering centred on seafood. Located a few steps from the port and the city beaches, it is the best place to buy fresh fish and seafood with the guarantee that it comes straight from the boats that operate in the Mediterranean. On Wednesdays, the Grao flea market fills the neighbourhood’s streets with varied goods.
facts: Fish and seafood from the port
The most direct connection with the boats that fish in the Mediterranean
The offering changes with the closed seasons and the season of each species
The most seafaring neighbourhood in Valencia, next to the Port and the Fishermen’s Lonja
Varied goods in the streets of El Grao every Wednesday morning

items.title: Ceramics · Manises and Paterna
items.body: Valencia has a ceramic tradition of more than 800 years. The municipalities of Manises and Paterna are the most important production centres. Look for hand-painted tiles, earthenware tableware and decorative ceramic figures with traditional Valencian motifs.
facts: Shops in the historic centre · Manises (10 km)

items.title: Silk · Ensedarte and artisans
items.body: Valencian silk has Moorish roots and was for centuries the most important industry in the city. La Lonja de la Seda is a World Heritage Site. Today, artisans such as Ensedarte revive the tradition with hand-painted silk accessories.
facts: El Carmen district · Plaza del Mercado

items.title: Fans · Vibenca and Carbonell
items.body: The Valencian fan is a craft unique in the world with centuries of history. The houses of Vibenca and Carbonell are the references for artisan fan-making in Valencia: pieces hand-painted on silk or lace over wooden or mother-of-pearl ribs.

items.title: Porcelain · Lladró
items.body: Lladró is the best-known art porcelain brand in Spain and one of the most internationally known in the world. Founded in Valencia in 1953, its figures are collectables and works of art. The flagship store is on Calle Poeta Querol.

items.title: Goldsmithing · Peris Roca
items.body: Valencian jewellery and goldsmithing have a long artisan tradition. Peris Roca is one of the oldest jewellery houses in Valencia, with highly crafted pieces inspired by the ornamental motifs of Valencian historical heritage.

items.title: Huerta produce · Km 0
items.body: The municipal markets are the best place to buy artisan turrón, oranges from the huerta, extra virgin olive oil, wines of the Valencia and Utiel-Requena Designation of Origin, and other food products with designation of origin.

blocks.title: Tips for sustainable shopping in Valencia
items: Municipal markets open Monday to Saturday in the mornings: plan your visit before 14:00
The Central Market is the most photogenic but also the most crowded: go first thing to avoid the crowds
The Mercado de Colón is open every day including weekends: the only one with continuous hours until 21:00
Buy local crafts instead of industrially produced souvenirs: the economic impact is completely different
Huerta produce at the markets is fresher and cheaper than in supermarkets
The Rastro de Tarongers (Sundays) is the best second-hand flea market for finding unique pieces at a good price
